subject: chemistry
stem: The IUPAC name of (CH3)2CH-CH(OH)-CH3 is:
explanation: The longest carbon chain carrying the OH group has four carbons, so the parent is butane. Numbering starts from the end that gives the OH group the lowest locant, which is 2, and the methyl branch then sits on carbon 3. The name is therefore 3-methylbutan-2-ol.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: IUPAC nomenclature of alcohols

subject: chemistry
stem: Which alcohol gives an immediate turbidity when shaken with Lucas reagent (concentrated HCl with anhydrous ZnCl2) at room temperature?
explanation: Lucas reagent converts an alcohol into an alkyl chloride, which separates as a cloudy layer. Tertiary alcohols react through a stable carbocation and turn turbid at once. Secondary alcohols take several minutes, and primary alcohols show no turbidity at room temperature.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: Chemical reactions of alcohols (classification by Lucas test)

subject: chemistry
stem: Propene is treated with diborane (B2H6) in tetrahydrofuran, and the intermediate is then oxidised with alkaline hydrogen peroxide. The major organic product is:
explanation: Hydroboration places boron on the less hindered terminal carbon and hydrogen on the internal carbon, an anti-Markovnikov addition. Alkaline hydrogen peroxide then replaces boron with OH, giving the primary alcohol propan-1-ol. Acid-catalysed hydration of propene gives the Markovnikov product propan-2-ol instead.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: Preparation of alcohols from alkenes (hydroboration-oxidation)

subject: chemistry
stem: Which of the following is the most acidic compound?
explanation: Phenol loses a proton to form the phenoxide ion, whose negative charge is delocalised into the benzene ring by resonance. Alkoxide ions from ethanol and cyclohexanol have no such stabilisation, and water is itself more acidic than alcohols. The phenoxide route makes phenol the most acidic of these four.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: Acidic nature of phenol

subject: chemistry
stem: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (A) Reimer-Tiemann reaction (B) Kolbe's reaction (C) Williamson synthesis (D) Hydroboration-oxidation of propene. List-II: (I) Propan-1-ol (II) Salicylaldehyde (III) Salicylic acid (IV) Methoxyethane. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
explanation: Reimer-Tiemann treats phenol with chloroform and NaOH, introducing a CHO group ortho to the OH to give salicylaldehyde. Kolbe's reaction passes CO2 through sodium phenoxide under pressure, giving salicylic acid. Williamson synthesis of sodium methoxide with bromoethane gives methoxyethane, and hydroboration-oxidation of propene gives propan-1-ol.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: Preparation of phenols; Reimer-Tiemann and Kolbe reactions; Williamson synthesis

subject: chemistry
stem: 2-Methylbutan-2-ol is heated with excess concentrated sulphuric acid. Which alkene is the major product?
explanation: Dehydration proceeds through a tertiary carbocation formed after protonation and loss of water. Removal of a proton from the neighbouring carbon gives the more substituted, more stable alkene, which is the Saytzeff product. Here that is 2-methylbut-2-ene, the trisubstituted alkene, formed in greater amount than the terminal isomer.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: Dehydration of alcohols to alkenes (Saytzeff rule)

subject: chemistry
stem: Ethylmagnesium bromide reacts with methanal (formaldehyde), and the product is hydrolysed with dilute acid. The alcohol formed is:
explanation: The ethyl group adds to the carbonyl carbon of methanal, and hydrolysis gives a primary alcohol. Two carbons from the ethyl group and one from formaldehyde give three carbons in total, so the product is CH3CH2CH2OH, propan-1-ol. Propan-2-ol would instead come from methylmagnesium bromide and ethanal.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: Preparation of alcohols using Grignard reagents

subject: chemistry
stem: Arrange the following in order of increasing acidity: (A) p-Nitrophenol (B) Ethanol (C) Phenol (D) Water.
explanation: Ethanol is the weakest acid of the four, and water is a stronger acid than ethanol because ethoxide is a stronger base than hydroxide. Phenol is far more acidic than water because its phenoxide is resonance stabilised. A para-nitro group withdraws electron density and stabilises the phenoxide further, so p-nitrophenol is the most acidic.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: Acidic nature of phenol and effect of substituents

subject: chemistry
stem: Consider the following statements about the dehydration of ethanol with concentrated sulphuric acid. I. At about 443 K, ethene is the major product. II. At about 413 K, diethyl ether is the major product. III. At 443 K, diethyl ether is the major product. Which statements are correct?
explanation: Ethanol forms an alkyl hydrogen sulphate, which then reacts with a second alcohol molecule at lower temperature to give diethyl ether. At about 443 K, intramolecular dehydration takes over and ethene is the product. Statement III reverses the two temperature outcomes, so it is false.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: Dehydration of ethanol to ethene and to diethyl ether

subject: chemistry
stem: Phenol is treated with bromine water at room temperature without any catalyst. The major organic product is:
explanation: The OH group strongly activates the ring for electrophilic substitution, so bromine enters at both ortho positions and the para position without a Lewis acid catalyst. The product is 2,4,6-tribromophenol, which separates as a white precipitate and is the classic test for phenol. Bromobenzene would need a catalyst and is not formed here.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: Electrophilic substitution reactions of phenol

subject: chemistry
stem: 2-Methyl-2-methoxypropane, (CH3)3C-O-CH3, is treated with one equivalent of cold concentrated HI. Which pair of products is formed?
explanation: Ether cleavage begins with protonation of the ether oxygen. Because one side is tertiary, the C-O bond to the tert-butyl group breaks by an SN1 route, giving the stable tert-butyl cation, which iodide captures. The methyl side remains as methanol, since SN2 attack at a tertiary carbon is not possible.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: Reactions of ethers: cleavage by HI

subject: chemistry
stem: Consider the following statements about alcohols, phenols and ethers. I. Ethanol boils at a higher temperature than methoxymethane, although both have molecular mass 46. II. Phenol is a stronger acid than ethanol. III. Phenol liberates carbon dioxide from sodium bicarbonate solution. Which statements are correct?
explanation: Ethanol forms intermolecular hydrogen bonds, which raise its boiling point to about 78 C, while methoxymethane has no O-H group and boils at about -24 C. Phenol is more acidic than ethanol because its phenoxide ion is resonance stabilised. Phenol is too weak an acid to release CO2 from sodium bicarbonate, so statement III is false.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: Physical properties of alcohols and phenols; acidic nature of phenol

subject: chemistry
stem: Assertion (A): 2-Methylpropan-2-ol is dehydrated more readily than ethanol under the same acidic conditions. Reason (R): The tertiary carbocation formed from 2-methylpropan-2-ol is stabilised by hyperconjugation and by the electron-releasing inductive effect of three alkyl groups.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

explanation: Tertiary alcohols lose water through a carbocation that is stabilised by hyperconjugation and by the inductive effect of three alkyl groups, so milder conditions are enough. Primary alcohols such as ethanol do not pass through a comparably stable cation, which is why they need higher temperatures. The stability of the tertiary cation therefore explains why the tertiary alcohol dehydrates more readily.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: Dehydration of alcohols and carbocation stability

subject: chemistry
stem: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (A) Propan-1-ol with pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC) (B) Propan-1-ol with acidified potassium dichromate (C) Propan-2-ol with acidified potassium dichromate (D) Ethanol heated with excess concentrated H2SO4 at about 443 K. List-II: (I) Propanone (II) Propanoic acid (III) Propanal (IV) Ethene. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
explanation: PCC stops the oxidation of a primary alcohol at the aldehyde, giving propanal. Acidified dichromate carries a primary alcohol on to the carboxylic acid, propanoic acid. Oxidation of a secondary alcohol gives a ketone, propanone, and hot concentrated acid dehydrates ethanol to ethene.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: Oxidation of alcohols (primary, secondary)

subject: chemistry
stem: 1-Methylcyclohexene is treated with diborane in tetrahydrofuran, and the intermediate is oxidised with alkaline hydrogen peroxide. Which is the major product?
explanation: Boron adds to the less substituted alkene carbon, which is the CH carbon, and hydrogen goes to the methyl-bearing carbon, an anti-Markovnikov hydroboration. Oxidation then replaces boron with OH on the same carbon. The product is therefore 2-methylcyclohexan-1-ol, with the OH on the former CH carbon next to the methyl group.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: Preparation of alcohols from alkenes (hydroboration-oxidation)

subject: chemistry
stem: Methyl tert-butyl ether, (CH3)3C-O-CH3, is to be made by the Williamson synthesis. Which pair of reagents gives the best yield?
explanation: The Williamson synthesis is an SN2 reaction, so the alkyl halide should be methyl or primary. A tertiary alkyl halide undergoes mainly elimination when attacked by a strong base such as an alkoxide. Using tert-butoxide as the nucleophile and iodomethane as the electrophile keeps the bulky group on the alkoxide side and gives the ether.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: Preparation of ethers by Williamson synthesis

subject: chemistry
stem: 2-Methylpropene is treated with water in the presence of a dilute acid catalyst. Which alcohol is the major product?
explanation: The acid adds a proton to the terminal CH2 carbon, which leaves the more stable tertiary carbocation as the intermediate. Water then attacks that carbon, and this Markovnikov addition gives 2-methylpropan-2-ol. The anti-Markovnikov primary alcohol is not the major product under acid catalysis.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: Preparation of alcohols by acid-catalysed hydration of alkenes

subject: chemistry
stem: Which of the following compounds is optically active?
explanation: A carbon bonded to four different groups is a chiral centre. In 2-chlorobutane, carbon 2 carries H, Cl, CH3 and CH2CH3, so the molecule is chiral and optically active. The other three compounds have no stereocentre.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes: Stereochemistry of haloalkanes (chirality)

subject: chemistry
stem: Arrange the following alkyl bromides in decreasing order of their rate of SN2 reaction with iodide ion in acetone: (A) 2-Bromo-2-methylpropane (B) Bromomethane (C) 2-Bromopropane (D) Bromoethane.
explanation: In SN2 the nucleophile attacks from the back of the carbon, so crowding at that carbon slows the reaction. The reactivity order is methyl greater than primary, greater than secondary, greater than tertiary. Bromomethane reacts fastest, then bromoethane, then 2-bromopropane, and 2-bromo-2-methylpropane barely reacts by SN2.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes: Nucleophilic substitution (SN2) and steric effects

subject: chemistry
stem: Consider the following statements about nucleophilic substitution of haloalkanes. I. An SN2 reaction of a chiral haloalkane proceeds with inversion of configuration. II. An SN1 reaction of a chiral haloalkane gives a nearly racemic product. III. Tertiary haloalkanes react mainly by SN2 with strong nucleophiles such as hydroxide ion. Which statements are correct?
explanation: SN2 is a single concerted step with backside attack, which inverts the configuration at the carbon. SN1 proceeds through a planar carbocation that the nucleophile can attack from either face, giving near racemisation. Tertiary carbons are too crowded for SN2, so they react by SN1 or by elimination with strong bases.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes: Mechanisms of SN1 and SN2 reactions

subject: chemistry
stem: 2-Bromobutane is heated with alcoholic potassium hydroxide. Which alkene is the major product?
explanation: Alcoholic KOH removes HBr by elimination. Following the Saytzeff rule, the proton is lost from the carbon that gives the more substituted and more stable alkene. The internal alkene but-2-ene, which is disubstituted, therefore predominates over the terminal but-1-ene.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes: Dehydrohalogenation and the Saytzeff rule

subject: chemistry
stem: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (A) Finkelstein reaction (B) Swarts reaction (C) Wurtz reaction (D) Dow process. List-II: (I) Sodium metal in dry ether (II) Sodium iodide in dry acetone (III) Silver fluoride or mercurous fluoride (IV) Sodium hydroxide at about 623 K and high pressure, followed by acidification. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
explanation: The Finkelstein reaction exchanges chlorine or bromine for iodine using NaI in acetone, and the insoluble NaCl drives the change. The Swarts reaction uses AgF or Hg2F2 to introduce fluorine. Wurtz coupling joins two alkyl halides with sodium in dry ether, and the Dow process converts chlorobenzene to phenol with NaOH at high temperature and pressure.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes: Methods of preparation; conversion of chlorobenzene to phenol

subject: chemistry
stem: Ethylmagnesium bromide is treated with water. The organic product is:
explanation: Grignard reagents are strong bases and take a proton from water, so the ethyl group becomes an alkane. The C-Mg bond is replaced by a C-H bond, which gives ethane. Ethanol would form only if the Grignard reagent reacted with a carbonyl compound or with oxygen.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes: Reaction of haloalkanes with magnesium (Grignard reagents)

subject: chemistry
stem: Assertion (A): Chlorobenzene does not undergo nucleophilic substitution with aqueous sodium hydroxide under ordinary conditions. Reason (R): In chlorobenzene the C-Cl bond has partial double-bond character due to resonance, and the sp2-hybridised carbon attached to chlorine is more electronegative.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

explanation: The lone pair on chlorine conjugates with the ring, which shortens the C-Cl bond and gives it partial double-bond character, making it harder to break. The sp2 carbon is also more electronegative than an sp3 carbon, so it holds the bonding electrons more tightly. Together these effects explain why chlorobenzene resists nucleophilic substitution under ordinary conditions.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes: Nature of the C-X bond in haloarenes

subject: chemistry
stem: Consider the following statements about polyhalogen compounds. I. DDT is persistent in the environment and accumulates in the fatty tissues of organisms. II. Chlorofluorocarbons (freons) release chlorine free radicals in the stratosphere that catalyse the breakdown of ozone. III. Freons are chemically reactive in the lower atmosphere, which is why they are used as refrigerants. Which statements are correct?
explanation: DDT is a persistent organochlorine pesticide that is stored in fatty tissue, which is why its use was restricted. Freons are chemically inert in the lower atmosphere, so they reach the stratosphere, where UV light releases chlorine radicals that destroy ozone. Their inertness, not reactivity, is the reason they serve as refrigerants, so statement III is false.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes: Polyhalogen compounds (DDT and freons)

subject: chemistry
stem: Which of the following monosaccharides is a ketose?
explanation: Fructose has a ketone group (C=O) at C-2, so it is a ketohexose. Glucose, galactose and mannose each have an aldehyde group at C-1 and are aldohexoses.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 14 Biomolecules: Carbohydrates

subject: chemistry
stem: On hydrolysis, sucrose gives which pair of monosaccharides?
explanation: Sucrose is a disaccharide of alpha-D-glucose and beta-D-fructose joined by a glycosidic bond. Hydrolysis breaks this bond and releases one glucose and one fructose, which is why the mixture is called invert sugar.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 14 Biomolecules: Carbohydrates

subject: chemistry
stem: Sucrose is a non-reducing sugar. Which feature of its structure explains this?

options.text: It has a free aldehyde group at C-1 of its glucose unit
It exists only in the open-chain ketose form
The glycosidic bond joins the anomeric carbons of glucose and fructose, so no free aldehyde or ketone group can form
It contains no hydroxyl groups at all

explanation: In sucrose, C-1 of alpha-glucose is joined to C-2 of beta-fructose, so neither anomeric carbon is free to open into a carbonyl group. Reducing sugars need a free aldehyde or ketone, or a ring that can open to one, to reduce Fehling's or Tollens' reagent.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 14 Biomolecules: Carbohydrates

subject: chemistry
stem: How does amylopectin differ structurally from amylose?

options.text: It is made of beta-D-glucose units joined by beta-1,4 linkages
It is made of fructose units joined by alpha-1,2 linkages
It is an unbranched chain of alpha-1,4 linkages
It has alpha-1,6 glycosidic branch points in addition to alpha-1,4 linkages

explanation: Both are polymers of alpha-D-glucose. Amylose is essentially a linear chain of alpha-1,4 linkages, while amylopectin is branched at alpha-1,6 linkages.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 14 Biomolecules: Carbohydrates

subject: chemistry
stem: Cellulose is a polymer of which monosaccharide, and what linkage joins its units?

options.text: Beta-D-glucose units joined by beta-1,4 glycosidic linkages
Alpha-D-glucose units joined by alpha-1,4 glycosidic linkages
Beta-D-fructose units joined by beta-1,2 glycosidic linkages
Alpha-D-galactose units joined by alpha-1,6 glycosidic linkages

explanation: Cellulose is an unbranched chain of beta-D-glucose units linked by beta-1,4 bonds. The beta linkage keeps the chains straight so they pack into strong fibres, and humans cannot digest it because they lack an enzyme that hydrolyses beta-glycosidic bonds.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 14 Biomolecules: Carbohydrates

subject: chemistry
stem: Glycogen is the storage polysaccharide of animals. It is structurally most similar to which polysaccharide?
explanation: Glycogen is a highly branched polymer of alpha-D-glucose, like amylopectin, but it branches more often, roughly every 8 to 12 residues. Cellulose is linear and beta-linked, and amylose is essentially unbranched.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 14 Biomolecules: Carbohydrates

subject: chemistry
stem: In aqueous solution at its isoelectric point, glycine exists mainly as which species?
explanation: An amino acid exists as a zwitterion, carrying a protonated amino group and a deprotonated carboxylate group. At the isoelectric point the net charge is zero, and the dominant form of glycine is the zwitterion H3N+-CH2-COO-.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 14 Biomolecules: Proteins

subject: chemistry
stem: In the alpha-helix, the secondary structure of a protein is stabilised mainly by which interaction?

options.text: Ionic bonds between arginine and aspartate side chains
Van der Waals forces between adjacent helices
Hydrogen bonds between the C=O of one residue and the N-H of the residue four positions along the chain

explanation: In an alpha-helix, each backbone C=O group hydrogen-bonds with the N-H group of the amino acid four residues ahead, which holds the coil together. Disulfide bonds and salt bridges between side chains stabilise tertiary structure, not secondary structure.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 14 Biomolecules: Proteins

subject: chemistry
stem: Which statement about enzymes is correct?

options.text: Enzymes are consumed in the reaction they catalyse
Enzymes are highly specific for their substrates
Enzymes change the equilibrium constant of the reaction
Enzymes are most active at very high temperatures

explanation: Enzymes are biological catalysts with high substrate specificity. They lower the activation energy, are not consumed, and do not change the equilibrium constant. Their activity falls at very high temperatures because the protein denatures.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 14 Biomolecules: Enzymes

subject: chemistry
stem: Match List-I (vitamin) with List-II (deficiency disease). List-I: (A) Vitamin B1 (B) Vitamin C (C) Vitamin D (D) Vitamin K. List-II: (I) Rickets (II) Scurvy (III) Beriberi (IV) Delayed blood clotting. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
explanation: Vitamin B1 deficiency causes beriberi (III). Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy (II). Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets in children (I). Vitamin K deficiency delays blood clotting (IV), so the correct pairing is (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV).
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 14 Biomolecules: Vitamins

subject: chemistry
stem: Which vitamin is synthesised in the human skin when it is exposed to sunlight?
explanation: A precursor (7-dehydrocholesterol) in the skin is converted to vitamin D3 by ultraviolet light from sunlight. Vitamin C is not synthesised by humans and must come from food such as citrus fruit.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 14 Biomolecules: Vitamins

subject: chemistry
stem: Which pair correctly gives the sugar and a nitrogenous base found in RNA?
explanation: RNA nucleotides contain ribose and the bases adenine, guanine, cytosine and uracil. DNA contains deoxyribose and thymine in place of uracil, so the thymine options describe DNA, not RNA.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 14 Biomolecules: Nucleic Acids

subject: chemistry
stem: A DNA double helix has one strand written 5'-ATGC-3'. What is the sequence of the complementary strand, written 5' to 3'?
explanation: The strands run antiparallel, and A pairs with T while G pairs with C. The partner strand is 3'-TACG-5', which read 5' to 3' gives 5'-GCAT-3'. Writing TACG without reversing its direction is the common error.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 14 Biomolecules: Nucleic Acids

subject: chemistry
stem: Which reagents are used in the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction to convert a carboxylic acid into an alpha-bromo acid?

options.text: Br2 with a little red phosphorus

explanation: Red phosphorus converts a small amount of the acid into an acyl bromide, which enolises readily, and bromine then substitutes at the alpha-carbon. Br2 with FeBr3 is used for ring bromination of arenes, not for this reaction.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 12 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids: Carboxylic acids, alpha-halogenation (HVZ)

subject: chemistry
stem: Ethanal is treated with dilute aqueous NaOH at room temperature. Which product is formed?
explanation: Ethanal has alpha-hydrogens. Hydroxide removes one to form an enolate, which attacks the carbonyl carbon of a second ethanal molecule. The aldol product is 3-hydroxybutanal, which can later dehydrate to but-2-enal on heating.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 12 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids: Aldol condensation

subject: chemistry
stem: Which reagents are used for the Wolff-Kishner reduction of a carbonyl compound to a methylene group?

options.text: Hydrazine followed by heating with KOH in ethylene glycol

explanation: Hydrazine forms a hydrazone with the carbonyl group. Heating this with KOH in a high-boiling solvent such as ethylene glycol releases nitrogen and gives the CH2 group. Zn-Hg with HCl is the Clemmensen reduction, which uses strong acid instead of base.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 12 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids: Reduction reactions

subject: chemistry
stem: Which carbonyl compound is most reactive towards nucleophilic addition, for example with HCN?
explanation: Electron-donating alkyl or aryl groups reduce the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon, and bulky groups add steric hindrance. Formaldehyde has no alkyl group and is the most reactive; acetaldehyde is next, then acetone, and benzophenone is the least reactive.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 12 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids: Nucleophilic addition reactions

subject: chemistry
stem: Ethanal is warmed with excess iodine in aqueous NaOH. Which yellow precipitate is formed?
explanation: Ethanal contains a CH3-CO- unit. The iodoform reaction cleaves this unit in excess iodine and alkali, producing the yellow crystalline precipitate CHI3 and a carboxylate salt.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 12 Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids: Haloform (iodoform) reaction

subject: chemistry
stem: Assertion: Chlorobenzene is far less reactive than ethyl chloride towards nucleophilic substitution. Reason: In chlorobenzene the C-Cl bond has partial double-bond character due to resonance, making it shorter and stronger. Choose the correct option.

options.text: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason does not explain Assertion
Assertion is true but Reason is false
Assertion is false but Reason is true
Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason correctly explains Assertion

explanation: A lone pair on chlorine overlaps with the pi system of the ring, giving the C-Cl bond partial double-bond character. The bond is shorter and stronger and resists cleavage, which explains the lower reactivity. Aryl halides also resist SN1 because the phenyl cation is unstable.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 10 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes: Nature of C-X bond

subject: chemistry
stem: Which order of reactivity of alkyl halides in an SN2 reaction is correct?
explanation: In SN2 reactions the leaving group must depart easily. Iodide is the largest and most polarisable halide ion and the weakest base, so it is the best leaving group. Fluoride is the poorest, giving the order RI > RBr > RCl > RF.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 10 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes: Nucleophilic substitution (SN1 and SN2)

subject: chemistry
stem: Methylmagnesium iodide, prepared from CH3I and magnesium in dry ether, is treated with ethanal. The product after dilute acid hydrolysis is:
explanation: CH3MgI adds to the carbonyl carbon of ethanal (CH3CHO), giving a magnesium alkoxide. Acid hydrolysis gives CH3CH(OH)CH3, which is propan-2-ol, a secondary alcohol.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 10 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes: Chemical reactions (reaction with magnesium)

subject: chemistry
stem: Benzenediazonium chloride is warmed with cuprous chloride dissolved in hydrochloric acid. The major organic product is:
explanation: This is the Sandmeyer reaction. Copper(I) chloride catalyses replacement of the diazonium group by chlorine, with N2 gas released, giving chlorobenzene. Benzonitrile needs CuCN, and benzene is obtained with hypophosphorous acid.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 13 Amines: Chemical reactions of diazonium salts (Sandmeyer reaction)

subject: chemistry
stem: Benzenediazonium chloride is added to phenol in cold alkaline solution (pH about 9 to 10). The main product is:
explanation: This is an azo coupling reaction. The diazonium ion is a weak electrophile and attacks the activated para position of the phenoxide ion, forming p-hydroxyazobenzene, which contains the -N=N- azo linkage. The alkaline medium is needed to generate the phenoxide ion.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 13 Amines: Coupling reactions of diazonium salts

subject: chemistry
stem: Which amine gives a yellow, oily N-nitrosoamine when treated with sodium nitrite and hydrochloric acid at low temperature?
explanation: Secondary amines react with nitrous acid to give N-nitrosamines, which are yellow oily liquids insoluble in water. Methylamine gives methanol and N2, tertiary amines do not form a nitrosamine, and aniline forms a diazonium salt.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 13 Amines: Reaction with nitrous acid

subject: chemistry
stem: The ground-state electronic configuration of chromium (atomic number 24) is:
explanation: Chromium moves one electron from 4s to 3d to get a half-filled 3d⁵ subshell, which has extra stability from exchange energy. So its configuration is [Ar] 3d⁵ 4s¹, not the one predicted by the simple filling order.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements, Electronic configurations of d-block elements

subject: chemistry
stem: The spin-only magnetic moment of the Ti³⁺ ion (atomic number 22), in Bohr magnetons, is:
explanation: Ti³⁺ is 3d¹ with one unpaired electron. Spin-only moment is √(n(n+2)) with n = 1 unpaired electron, which gives √3 ≈ 1.73 BM.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements, Magnetic properties of transition elements

subject: chemistry
stem: The spin-only magnetic moment of the free Fe²⁺ ion (atomic number 26), in Bohr magnetons, is closest to:
explanation: Fe²⁺ is 3d⁶, which has four unpaired electrons in the free ion. Spin-only moment √(4×6) = √24 ≈ 4.90 BM.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements, Magnetic properties of transition elements

subject: chemistry
stem: Which of the following aqueous ions is colourless?
explanation: Colour in transition metal ions comes from d-d transitions, which need electrons in d orbitals. Sc³⁺ is 3d⁰, so it has no d-d transition and is colourless, while Ti³⁺, V³⁺ and Fe²⁺ are coloured.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements, Colour of transition metal ions

subject: chemistry
stem: When potassium permanganate is reduced in a neutral aqueous solution, the manganese product is:
explanation: The reduction product depends on the medium: Mn²⁺ in acid (five electrons gained), MnO₂ in neutral solution (three electrons gained, Mn in +4), and manganate MnO₄²⁻ in strongly alkaline solution (one electron gained). In neutral solution the brown precipitate is MnO₂.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements, Potassium permanganate

subject: chemistry
stem: In acidic medium, one mole of dichromate ion (Cr₂O₇²⁻) oxidises how many moles of Fe²⁺ to Fe³⁺?
explanation: Each Cr₂O₇²⁻ is reduced to 2Cr³⁺, which gains 6 electrons. Each Fe²⁺ loses one electron on oxidation to Fe³⁺, so 6 moles of Fe²⁺ are oxidised per mole of dichromate.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements, Potassium dichromate

subject: chemistry
stem: Which catalyst is used in the Contact process for manufacturing sulphuric acid?
explanation: In the Contact process, sulphur dioxide is oxidised to sulphur trioxide over vanadium(V) oxide. V₂O₅ works because vanadium switches between +5 and +4 oxidation states, which is typical of d-block catalysts. TiCl₄ belongs to Ziegler–Natta catalysis.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements, Catalytic properties of transition elements

subject: chemistry
stem: In aqueous solution Cu⁺ disproportionates, while Cu²⁺ is stable. The main reason is:

options.text: The high hydration enthalpy of Cu²⁺ more than compensates for the second ionisation enthalpy of copper
Cu⁺ has a higher hydration enthalpy than Cu²⁺
Cu⁺ has a half-filled d subshell
Cu⁺ is a stronger oxidising agent than Cu²⁺

explanation: Cu⁺ is 3d¹⁰ and disproportionates as 2Cu⁺ → Cu + Cu²⁺. The Cu²⁺ ion has a very large hydration enthalpy, which offsets the energy needed to remove the second electron from copper, so Cu²⁺ is more stable in water.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements, Stability of copper oxidation states

subject: chemistry
stem: Actinoids show a wider range of oxidation states than lanthanoids. The main reason is:

options.text: 5f electrons are more effectively shielded than 4f electrons
Actinoid ions have lower ionisation enthalpies than lanthanoid ions
Actinoids have no electrons in 6d orbitals
The 5f, 6d and 7s energy levels are close, so more electrons take part in bonding

explanation: The 5f, 6d and 7s orbitals have similar energies, so several electrons can be used in bonding. The 5f electrons are less effectively shielded than 4f electrons, and this allows a wider spread of oxidation states than in the lanthanoids.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements, Actinoids

subject: chemistry
stem: In an acidic medium, MnO₄⁻ is reduced to Mn²⁺. How many moles of MnO₄⁻ are needed to oxidise 2.5 mol of Fe²⁺ to Fe³⁺?
explanation: Each MnO₄⁻ gains five electrons to become Mn²⁺, and each Fe²⁺ gives one electron. So 2.5 mol of Fe²⁺ supplies 2.5 mol of electrons, and 2.5 ÷ 5 = 0.5 mol of MnO₄⁻ is required.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 4 d- and f-Block Elements, Potassium permanganate

subject: chemistry
stem: Concentrated aqueous sodium chloride is electrolysed with inert electrodes. The products formed are:

options.text: H₂ at the anode and Na at the cathode
Cl₂ at the anode and H₂ at the cathode
O₂ at the anode and Na at the cathode
Cl₂ at the cathode and H₂ at the anode

explanation: At the cathode, water is reduced to H₂ and OH⁻, which is easier than reducing Na⁺. At the anode, chloride ions are oxidised to Cl₂ in concentrated solution, which is preferred over oxidising water to O₂.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part I, Ch 3 Electrochemistry, Electrolytic cells and Faraday laws

subject: chemistry
stem: Iron is galvanised by coating it with a metal so that the coating protects iron even when the surface is scratched. The metal is:
explanation: Zinc has a more negative standard electrode potential (−0.76 V) than iron (−0.44 V), so it corrodes first and acts as a sacrificial anode. A tin or nickel coating protects only while it is intact.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part I, Ch 3 Electrochemistry, Corrosion

subject: chemistry
stem: The standard electrode potential of Zn²⁺/Zn is −0.76 V. At 298 K, the potential of the Zn²⁺/Zn electrode in 0.1 M Zn²⁺ solution is closest to (take 2.303RT/F = 0.059 V):
explanation: By the Nernst equation, E = E° − (0.059/n) log(1/[Zn²⁺]) with n = 2. So E = −0.76 − (0.059/2) × log 10 = −0.76 − 0.03 = −0.79 V.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part I, Ch 3 Electrochemistry, Nernst equation

subject: chemistry
stem: For a cell reaction with n = 2, the standard EMF is 0.59 V at 298 K. Taking 2.303RT/F = 0.059 V, the equilibrium constant K is approximately:
explanation: At equilibrium E = 0, so the Nernst equation gives log K = nE°/0.059. Here log K = (2 × 0.59)/0.059 = 20, so K ≈ 10²⁰.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part I, Ch 3 Electrochemistry, Relation between EMF and equilibrium constant

subject: chemistry
stem: During discharge of a lead storage battery, the density of the sulphuric acid electrolyte:
explanation: Discharge gives Pb + PbO₂ + 2H₂SO₄ → 2PbSO₄ + 2H₂O. Sulphuric acid is consumed and water is produced, so the electrolyte becomes more dilute and its density falls. Checking the density is how the battery state is judged.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part I, Ch 3 Electrochemistry, Batteries: lead storage battery

subject: chemistry
stem: The conductivity of a 0.02 M solution of an electrolyte is 0.0024 S cm⁻¹ at 298 K. Its molar conductivity, in S cm² mol⁻¹, is:
explanation: Molar conductivity is Λm = κ × 1000 / c, where c is in mol L⁻¹. So Λm = 0.0024 × 1000 / 0.02 = 120 S cm² mol⁻¹, which is 1.2 × 10².
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part I, Ch 3 Electrochemistry, Molar conductivity

subject: chemistry
stem: The quantity of electricity needed to deposit 21.6 g of silver (molar mass 108 g mol⁻¹) from a solution of Ag⁺ is closest to (F = 96500 C mol⁻¹):
explanation: Moles of Ag = 21.6 / 108 = 0.2 mol, and each Ag⁺ needs one electron. So Q = 0.2 × 96500 = 19 300 C, which is 1.9 × 10⁴ C, as given by Faraday first law.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part I, Ch 3 Electrochemistry, Faraday laws of electrolysis

subject: chemistry
stem: Among Li, K, Na and Mg, which metal is the strongest reducing agent in aqueous solution? (Standard potentials: Li⁺/Li −3.05 V, K⁺/K −2.93 V, Na⁺/Na −2.71 V, Mg²⁺/Mg −2.37 V)
explanation: The most negative standard reduction potential means the metal is most easily oxidised, so it is the strongest reducing agent. Lithium is at −3.05 V, even though potassium is more reactive in air, because the Li⁺ ion is strongly hydrated in water.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part I, Ch 3 Electrochemistry, Standard electrode potential series

subject: chemistry
stem: The chelate effect makes [Ni(en)₃]²⁺ more stable than [Ni(NH₃)₆]²⁺. The main thermodynamic reason is:

options.text: en is a stronger field ligand with a larger Δo
The enthalpy of formation of [Ni(en)₃]²⁺ is much larger
The number of particles increases on chelation, giving a positive entropy change
Chelating ligands have a lower coordination number

explanation: In [Ni(NH₃)₆]²⁺ + 3 en → [Ni(en)₃]²⁺ + 6 NH₃, the number of particles rises from 4 to 7. This gives a positive entropy change, which makes the chelate complex more stable. The enthalpy change is similar for both complexes.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 5 Coordination Compounds, Chelate effect and stability of complexes

subject: chemistry
stem: The crystal field stabilisation energy of the high-spin octahedral [Cr(H₂O)₆]²⁺ ion (a d⁴ ion) is:
explanation: Water is a weak-field ligand, so the complex is high spin: t₂g³ e_g¹. CFSE = 3(−0.4 Δo) + 1(+0.6 Δo) = −0.6 Δo. The eg electron adds +0.6 Δo, which is why the answer is not −1.2 Δo.
ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 5 Coordination Compounds, Crystal field theory

subject: general_test
stem: Statements: All doctors are graduates. Some graduates are teachers. Conclusions: I. Some doctors are teachers. II. Some teachers are doctors. Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows

explanation: All doctors lie inside the set of graduates, but the graduates who are teachers may lie entirely outside the doctor set, so neither conclusion is forced. In a Venn diagram the teacher circle overlaps the graduate circle, while the doctor circle sits inside the graduate circle without touching the teacher circle.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical and Analytical Reasoning: Syllogisms (two statements, Venn logic)

subject: general_test
stem: Brush : Painter :: Pen : ?
explanation: A brush is the tool a painter uses, so the pair links a tool with the person who works with it. A pen is the tool a writer uses, so the answer is writer. Paper, ink and notebook are things used with a pen but do not name the person who uses it.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical and Analytical Reasoning: Analogy (word relationships)

subject: general_test
stem: If TABLE is coded as UBCMF, how is CHAIR coded?
explanation: Each letter of TABLE is moved one place forward in the alphabet to give UBCMF. Applying the same shift to CHAIR gives C to D, H to I, A to B, I to J and R to S, so the code is DIBJS.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical and Analytical Reasoning: Coding-decoding (letter shifts)

subject: general_test
stem: Ramesh has a son, Vikas, and a daughter, Gita. Vikas is married to Neha. How is Neha related to Gita?
explanation: Gita and Vikas are siblings, so Neha, who is married to Vikas, is the wife of Gita's brother. That relation is sister-in-law. Trace each marriage back to the sibling group before naming the relation.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical and Analytical Reasoning: Blood relations

subject: general_test
stem: Riya is facing north. She turns right twice, turning 90 degrees each time. Which direction is she facing now?
explanation: One right turn from north faces her east, and a second right turn from east faces her south. Two right turns make a half-turn, so she faces the opposite of her starting direction. Count right turns clockwise from the direction she is facing.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical and Analytical Reasoning: Direction sense

subject: general_test
stem: Arrange the following words in the order they would appear in a dictionary, from first to last: Tiger, Tablet, Table, Tail, Tab.
explanation: Dictionary order compares letters from left to right. Tab comes before Table because it is a prefix of it, and Table comes before Tablet for the same reason. Tablet comes before Tail because b precedes i at the third letter, and Tail comes before Tiger because a precedes i at the second letter.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical and Analytical Reasoning: Ranking and order (alphabetical ordering)

subject: general_test
stem: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (A) 2, 4, 8, 16 (B) 1, 4, 9, 16 (C) 1, 1, 2, 3 (D) 5, 10, 15, 20. List-II: (I) Squares of natural numbers (II) Constant ratio of 2 (III) Fibonacci sequence (IV) Constant difference of 5. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
explanation: 2, 4, 8, 16 doubles each time, so it has a constant ratio of 2 (A-II). 1, 4, 9, 16 are squares of 1 to 4 (B-I). 1, 1, 2, 3 is the Fibonacci sequence, where each term is the sum of the two before it (C-III). 5, 10, 15, 20 rises by a constant difference of 5 (D-IV).
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical and Analytical Reasoning: Number series and patterns (match)

subject: general_test
stem: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (A) All A are B (B) No A is B (C) Some A are B (D) All B are A. List-II: (I) A and B overlap partially (II) A and B are disjoint (III) A lies entirely within B (IV) B lies entirely within A. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
explanation: All A are B means circle A lies inside circle B (A-III). No A is B means the two circles are disjoint (B-II). Some A are B means the circles overlap partially (C-I). All B are A means circle B lies inside circle A (D-IV).
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical and Analytical Reasoning: Syllogisms (Venn logic of All, No, Some)

subject: general_test
stem: Five persons P, Q, R, S and T sit around a circular table, equidistant from each other and all facing the centre. P sits immediately to the right of Q. S sits second to the left of P. R does not sit next to S. Which person sits next to both Q and R?
explanation: Place Q, then P immediately after Q, so S sits two places before P on Q's other side. R cannot sit next to S, so R sits beside P and T sits between R and S. P is the only person adjacent to both Q and R.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical and Analytical Reasoning: Seating arrangement (circular)

subject: general_test
stem: Five persons P, Q, R, S and T sit in a single row facing north. Left and right are taken as seen by an observer facing the row. T sits at one of the two ends. P sits second to the right of T. Q sits immediately to the right of R. Who sits second to the left of Q?
explanation: T must be at an end, and P two places to its right forces T to the left end with P in the middle. Q sits immediately right of R, which leaves only the fourth and fifth places for them, so S is in the second place. Second to the left of Q is therefore P.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical and Analytical Reasoning: Seating arrangement (linear)

subject: general_test
stem: In a class of 40 students, Neha ranks 12th from the top. Rohit ranks 5 places below Neha. What is Rohit's rank from the bottom?
explanation: Rohit's rank from the top is 12 + 5 = 17. His rank from the bottom is 40 - 17 + 1 = 24, because a rank from one end plus the rank from the other end minus one equals the total number of students.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical and Analytical Reasoning: Ranking and order (rank from both ends)

subject: general_test
stem: If 15 March 2026 falls on a Sunday, what day of the week will 15 April 2026 be?
explanation: From 15 March to 15 April is 31 days: 16 days remain in March (16 to 31) and 15 days run into April (1 to 15). Since 31 leaves a remainder of 3 when divided by 7, the weekday moves forward by 3 days, so Sunday becomes Wednesday.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical and Analytical Reasoning: Calendars (odd days)

subject: general_test
stem: Statement: The school has announced that all classes will be held online from tomorrow. Assumptions: I. Students have access to devices and a working internet connection. II. The school will reopen for physical classes next month. Which assumption is implicit in the statement?

options.text: Both assumptions I and II are implicit

explanation: An announcement of online classes only works if students can reach the lessons, so assumption I is taken for granted. Assumption II concerns a future decision that the announcement does not depend on, so it is not implicit. An implicit assumption is a condition the speaker must believe for the statement to make sense.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical and Analytical Reasoning: Statement and assumption

subject: general_test
stem: Statement: Several guests at a wedding feast fell ill after eating food from the same caterer. Courses of action: I. The health department should inspect the caterer's kitchen and food storage. II. All wedding feasts in the city should be banned for a year. III. The guests should be asked to avoid weddings. Which course(s) of action follow?
explanation: A course of action should address the stated problem in proportion to it, and inspecting the source of contamination does that directly. Banning all weddings, or asking guests to avoid them, punishes many people for one caterer's failure. A course is rejected when it is disproportionate or aimed at the wrong people.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical and Analytical Reasoning: Course of action

subject: general_test
stem: Statement: Only those students who score above 90 per cent are selected for the advanced programme. Ravi was selected for the advanced programme. Conclusions: I. Ravi scored above 90 per cent. II. All students who score above 90 per cent are selected for the advanced programme.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows

explanation: 'Only those who score above 90 per cent are selected' means selection implies a score above 90 per cent, so Ravi's score is above 90 (I). Conclusion II reverses the condition, and 'only' does not say that everyone above 90 per cent is selected. Read 'only those who' as a one-way condition.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical and Analytical Reasoning: Statement and conclusion (the word 'only')

subject: general_test
stem: Ajay is taller than Bina. Bina is taller than Chirag. Divya is shorter than Chirag but taller than Esha. Arrange the five persons from the tallest to the shortest.
explanation: Chain the comparisons: Ajay > Bina > Chirag from the first two clues, and Chirag > Divya > Esha from the third. Combining the chains gives one full order. Check each option against every clue, since one wrong adjacent pair rules it out.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical and Analytical Reasoning: Ranking and order (height comparisons)

subject: general_test
stem: Statements: Some pens are inks. All inks are liquids. No liquid is a solid. Conclusions: I. Some pens are not solids. II. No pen is a solid. III. Some liquids are pens. Which conclusions follow?

options.text: Conclusions I, II and III follow

explanation: Some pens are inks, and every ink is a liquid, so those pens are liquids. Since no liquid is a solid, those pens are not solids (I), and the same pens show that some liquids are pens (III). Pens outside the ink group may still be solids, so II does not follow.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical and Analytical Reasoning: Syllogisms (three statements, Venn logic)

subject: general_test
stem: Five books, P, Q, R, S and T, are placed on a shelf from left to right. S is at the left end. P is immediately to the right of R. Q is to the right of P but not next to P. Which arrangement from left to right is correct?
explanation: S fixes the first place. P must sit immediately after R, and P in the fourth place would push Q beyond the fifth place, so R is in the second place and P in the third. Q must be in the fifth place to be right of P without touching it, which leaves T in the fourth place: S, R, P, T, Q.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical and Analytical Reasoning: Seating and arrangement (linear, ordering by clues)

subject: general_test
stem: What is the total number of students in a class? Statement I: The ratio of boys to girls is 3 : 2. Statement II: There are 18 boys in the class. Which option is correct?

options.text: Statement II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not
Both statements together are sufficient, but neither statement alone is sufficient

explanation: The ratio alone gives no actual head count, and 18 boys alone does not give the number of girls. Together, 3 parts equal 18 boys, so one part is 6, girls are 2 x 6 = 12, and the total is 30. Data sufficiency asks whether the data fixes the answer, not whether you can compute it.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical and Analytical Reasoning: Data sufficiency

subject: general_test
stem: Ravi starts from point O and walks 4 m north. He turns left and walks 3 m. He turns left again and walks 4 m. He then turns right and walks 6 m. In which direction, and how far, is Ravi from O?
explanation: Walking north, turning left to face west, turning left again to face south, and then turning right to face west. The 4 m north and 4 m south moves cancel, while the westward moves total 3 + 6 = 9 m. Track the facing direction after each turn and net the north-south and east-west moves separately.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical and Analytical Reasoning: Direction sense (multi-turn trace)

subject: general_test
stem: After 4 o'clock, at what time do the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock first coincide?
explanation: At 4 : m, the hour hand is 120 + m/2 degrees from the twelve and the minute hand is 6m degrees, so they coincide when 6m = 120 + m/2. This gives 5.5m = 120, so m = 240/11 = 21 9/11 minutes. The minute hand gains 5.5 degrees per minute on the hour hand, starting from a 120-degree gap.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical and Analytical Reasoning: Clocks (hour and minute hand coincidence)

subject: general_test
stem: Which Schedule of the Constitution of India lists the languages recognised by the Constitution?
explanation: The Eighth Schedule of the Constitution lists the languages recognised by it, and it is the list used for official recognition of languages. The Fifth Schedule concerns administration of Scheduled Areas, the Seventh Schedule divides legislative subjects between the Union and the States, and the Tenth Schedule contains the anti-defection provisions.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Knowledge: Indian Constitution, Schedules

subject: general_test
stem: The SI unit of electrical resistance is:
explanation: Electrical resistance is measured in ohms, given by the ratio of voltage to current according to Ohm's law. The farad is the unit of capacitance, the henry is the unit of inductance and the tesla is the unit of magnetic flux density. Knowing which quantity each SI unit measures helps in elimination.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Knowledge: Science basics, SI units

subject: general_test
stem: Which vitamin does the human skin synthesise when it is exposed to sunlight?
explanation: Ultraviolet B radiation from sunlight helps the skin convert a precursor into vitamin D. Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium and maintain healthy bones. Vitamin A, vitamin K and vitamin C are obtained mainly from diet.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Knowledge: Human health and nutrition

subject: general_test
stem: The words 'socialist' and 'secular' were added to the Preamble of the Constitution of India by which amendment?
explanation: The 42nd Amendment of 1976 inserted 'socialist', 'secular' and 'integrity' into the Preamble, describing India as a sovereign socialist secular democratic republic. The 44th Amendment of 1978 is known for removing the right to property from the Fundamental Rights. The 73rd Amendment dealt with Panchayati Raj.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Knowledge: Indian Constitution, amendments

subject: general_test
stem: Under which Article of the Constitution of India can the President proclaim a National Emergency?
explanation: Article 352 empowers the President to proclaim a National Emergency on grounds of war, external aggression or armed rebellion. Article 356 provides for President's Rule in a State, Article 360 for a Financial Emergency, and Article 370 gave special status to Jammu and Kashmir, which was later modified. Each emergency provision addresses a different situation.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Knowledge: Emergency provisions of the Constitution

subject: general_test
stem:
Consider the following statements about the Constitution of India.
(A) The right to property was removed from Part III (Fundamental Rights) by the 44th Amendment.
(B) Directive Principles of State Policy are enforceable by courts.
(C) Dr. B. R. Ambedkar described Article 32 as the heart and soul of the Constitution.
(D) Fundamental Duties are listed in Part IVA of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above are correct? Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
explanation: The 44th Amendment removed the right to property from Part III and made it a legal right under Article 300A. Directive Principles are not enforceable in courts, which is why statement (B) is false, while Article 32 is the remedy Ambedkar called the heart and soul of the Constitution. Fundamental Duties appear in Part IVA under Article 51A.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Knowledge: Fundamental Rights, DPSP and Fundamental Duties

subject: general_test
stem: Which of the following is a direct tax levied in India?
explanation: A direct tax is paid by the person on whom it is legally imposed and cannot be shifted to another person, as in the case of income tax. Goods and Services Tax, customs duty and excise duty are indirect taxes, because they are levied on goods and services and can be passed on to the consumer. Students should learn this distinction for the economy section.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Knowledge: Indian economy, taxation basics

subject: general_test
stem: When zinc metal reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid, the gas evolved is:
explanation: Most metals above hydrogen in the reactivity series react with dilute acids to release hydrogen gas, and zinc is one of them. The reaction forms zinc chloride along with hydrogen. Oxygen and chlorine are not produced by this reaction, and carbon dioxide needs a carbonate rather than a metal.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Knowledge: Chemistry basics, metals and acids

subject: general_test
stem: The headquarters of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) are located in:
explanation: The IAEA, the United Nations body that promotes peaceful use of nuclear energy and safeguards against its military use, has its headquarters in Vienna, Austria. Geneva hosts the WHO and ILO, Paris hosts UNESCO and The Hague hosts the International Court of Justice. Headquarters locations of UN agencies are a frequent CUET question.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Knowledge: International organisations and their headquarters

subject: general_test
stem: The headquarters of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) is located in:
explanation: UNEP, which coordinates environmental activities within the United Nations system, has its headquarters in Nairobi, Kenya. New York hosts the UN Secretariat and UNDP, Rome hosts FAO, and Bonn hosts the secretariat of the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change. Remember the headquarters of each UN agency along with its mandate.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Knowledge: International organisations and their headquarters

subject: general_test
stem: The Great Stupa at Sanchi, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is located in which state?
explanation: The Great Stupa at Sanchi, built under the Mauryan and later Shunga rule, is a Buddhist monument in Madhya Pradesh. It is known for its carved gateways and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Bodh Gaya, where the Buddha attained enlightenment, is in Bihar.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Knowledge: Indian architecture and UNESCO heritage sites

subject: general_test
stem: The book 'The Discovery of India' was written by:
explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru wrote 'The Discovery of India' during his imprisonment in the Ahmednagar Fort in 1944, tracing the history and culture of the country. Gandhi wrote 'Hind Swaraj' and his autobiography, while Patel and Azad were leaders of the freedom movement who did not write this book. Keep famous books paired with their authors.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Knowledge: Books and authors

subject: general_test
stem:
Assertion (A): The President of India can be removed from office before the end of the term through impeachment.
Reason (R): Article 61 lays down a procedure under which a charge may be preferred by either House of Parliament and the other House investigates it.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

explanation: Under Article 61, the President can be removed only through impeachment for violation of the Constitution, and the procedure allows a charge to be preferred by either House. The other House then investigates the charge, so the procedure described in the reason is exactly how the removal in the assertion takes place. Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Knowledge: Constitution, President and impeachment

subject: general_test
stem:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I: (A) Sabarmati (B) Brahmaputra (C) Yamuna (D) Mahanadi.
List-II: (I) Guwahati (II) Cuttack (III) Ahmedabad (IV) Delhi.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
explanation: The Sabarmati flows past Ahmedabad in Gujarat, the Brahmaputra past Guwahati in Assam, the Yamuna past Delhi and the Mahanadi past Cuttack in Odisha. Only the second option pairs all four correctly. The other options swap rivers and cities; the first, for example, puts the Sabarmati at Guwahati and the Brahmaputra at Ahmedabad. Learn each major river with one or two cities on its banks.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Knowledge: Indian rivers and the cities on them

subject: general_test
stem:
Arrange the following constitutional amendments of India in the chronological order of their enactment.
(A) 73rd Amendment
(B) 1st Amendment
(C) 42nd Amendment
(D) 86th Amendment
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
explanation: The 1st Amendment was enacted in 1951, the 42nd in 1976, the 73rd in 1992 and the 86th in 2002. The chronological order is therefore B, C, A, D. Remembering the decade of major amendments helps in answering ordering questions.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Knowledge: Indian Constitution, amendments in order

subject: general_test
stem: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for the appointment of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?
explanation: Article 148 provides for the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, who audits the accounts of the Union and the States. Article 124 concerns the Supreme Court, Article 280 the Finance Commission and Article 324 the Election Commission. Learning the Article for each constitutional body helps in polity questions.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Knowledge: Constitutional bodies and their Articles

subject: general_test
stem: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for the constitution of a Finance Commission?
explanation: Article 280 requires the President to constitute a Finance Commission at regular intervals, which recommends the distribution of tax revenues between the Union and the States. Article 265 says no tax shall be levied except by authority of law, Article 300 deals with suits against the government and Article 324 with the Election Commission. Article 280 is the key provision for fiscal federalism.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Knowledge: Centre-State finance and constitutional bodies

subject: general_test
stem: The population of a town is 40,000. It increases by 15% in the first year and then decreases by 10% in the second year. What is the population at the end of the second year?
explanation: A 15% increase takes 40,000 to 46,000. A 10% decrease of 46,000 removes 4,600, leaving 41,400. Successive percentage changes apply to the new value each time, so the two percentages cannot simply be added to give 42,000.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT section, Quantitative Reasoning: Percentages and successive change

subject: general_test
stem: A 56-litre mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 5 : 2. How many litres of water must be added so that the ratio of milk to water becomes 5 : 4?
explanation: The mixture has 5 + 2 = 7 parts, so each part is 8 litres: milk is 40 litres and water is 16 litres. Milk stays at 40 litres, so a 5 : 4 ratio needs 32 litres of water. Water to add = 32 - 16 = 16 litres.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT section, Quantitative Reasoning: Ratio, proportion and mixtures

subject: general_test
stem: A dealer sells a radio for Rs 1,134 and incurs a loss of 10%. What is the cost price of the radio?
explanation: A loss of 10% means the selling price is 90% of the cost price. So the cost price is 1,134 / 0.90 = 1,260. Taking 10% off the selling price (giving 1,020) uses the wrong base.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT section, Quantitative Reasoning: Profit and loss

subject: general_test
stem: What is the difference between the compound interest and the simple interest on Rs 8,000 for 2 years at 5% per annum, compounded annually?
explanation: Simple interest = 8,000 x 5% x 2 = Rs 800. Compound interest also earns interest on the first year's interest, so CI = 8,000 x 1.05 x 1.05 - 8,000 = Rs 820. The difference of Rs 20 is 5% of the Rs 400 first-year interest, which is the interest on interest.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT section, Quantitative Reasoning: Simple and compound interest

subject: general_test
stem: Pipe P can fill a tank alone in 20 hours and pipe Q can fill it alone in 30 hours. Both pipes are opened together, but pipe P is closed after 6 hours. How many more hours will pipe Q take to fill the remaining tank?
explanation: Together the pipes fill 1/20 + 1/30 = 1/12 of the tank each hour. In 6 hours they fill 6/12 = 1/2 of the tank. Pipe Q fills 1/30 per hour, so the remaining 1/2 takes (1/2) / (1/30) = 15 hours.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT section, Quantitative Reasoning: Time and work

subject: general_test
stem: The average marks of 12 students in section A are 40, and the average marks of 18 students in section B are 55. What is the average marks of all 30 students taken together?
explanation: The total for section A is 12 x 40 = 480, and the total for section B is 18 x 55 = 990. The combined total is 1,470 over 30 students, so the average is 1,470 / 30 = 49. The simple average of 40 and 55 (47.5) ignores the different group sizes.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT section, Quantitative Reasoning: Averages

subject: general_test
stem: A vessel contains 36 litres of a mixture of milk and water in the ratio 7 : 2. How many litres of water must be added so that the ratio of milk to water becomes 7 : 3?
explanation: The 7 + 2 = 9 parts give 36 / 9 = 4 litres per part, so the vessel holds 28 litres of milk and 8 litres of water. Milk stays at 28 litres, so a 7 : 3 ratio needs 12 litres of water. Water to add = 12 - 8 = 4 litres.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT section, Quantitative Reasoning: Mixtures and alligation

subject: general_test
stem: Vessel A contains 40 litres of a milk-and-water mixture in the ratio 3 : 1. Vessel B contains 60 litres of a mixture in the ratio 1 : 2. Both are poured into an empty third vessel. What is the ratio of milk to water in the third vessel?
explanation: Vessel A holds 30 litres of milk and 10 litres of water. Vessel B holds 20 litres of milk and 40 litres of water. The third vessel therefore has 50 litres of milk and 50 litres of water, a ratio of 1 : 1, which is found by adding quantities rather than averaging the two ratios.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT section, Quantitative Reasoning: Mixtures and alligation

subject: general_test
stem: A rectangular park is 120 m long and 80 m wide. A path of uniform width 5 m is built inside the park along its entire boundary. What is the area of the path?
explanation: The inner rectangle (the area left after the path) is (120 - 10) x (80 - 10) = 110 x 70 = 7,700 m². The path is the full area minus this inner area: 120 x 80 - 7,700 = 9,600 - 7,700 = 1,900 m².
ncert_ref: CUET GAT section, Quantitative Reasoning: Mensuration (area and perimeter)

subject: general_test
stem: A cubical water tank has each edge measuring 6 metres. How many litres of water does it hold when full? (1 cubic metre = 1,000 litres)
explanation: The volume of a cube is edge x edge x edge = 6 x 6 x 6 = 216 cubic metres. Using 1 cubic metre = 1,000 litres, the capacity is 216 x 1,000 = 216,000 litres. Leaving out the conversion gives a unit error, not a valid answer.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT section, Quantitative Reasoning: Mensuration (volume)

subject: general_test
stem: A boat takes 5 hours to travel 30 km upstream and 3 hours to return 30 km downstream to the starting point. What is the speed of the boat in still water?
explanation: Upstream speed = 30 / 5 = 6 km/h and downstream speed = 30 / 3 = 10 km/h. The speed in still water is the average of the two, (6 + 10) / 2 = 8 km/h. The stream speed is (10 - 6) / 2 = 2 km/h, which is a different quantity.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT section, Quantitative Reasoning: Time, speed and distance (boats and streams)

subject: general_test
stem: A sum of money amounts to Rs 9,680 in 2 years at 10% per annum, compounded annually. What is the sum invested?
explanation: Amount = P x (1 + 10/100)^2 = P x 1.21, so P = 9,680 / 1.21 = Rs 8,000. Dividing by 1.1 only once gives Rs 8,800, which accounts for just one year of interest.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT section, Quantitative Reasoning: Simple and compound interest

subject: general_test
stem: What is the HCF of 84 and 126?
explanation: 84 = 2^2 x 3 x 7 and 126 = 2 x 3^2 x 7. The HCF takes the lowest power of each common prime, giving 2 x 3 x 7 = 42. The LCM would use the highest powers instead.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT section, Numerical Ability: HCF and LCM

subject: general_test
stem: Three bells ring at intervals of 12 minutes, 18 minutes and 20 minutes. All three ring together at 9:00 am. At what time will they next ring together?
explanation: The next joint ringing comes after the LCM of 12, 18 and 20. Since 12 = 2^2 x 3, 18 = 2 x 3^2 and 20 = 2^2 x 5, the LCM is 2^2 x 3^2 x 5 = 180 minutes, or 3 hours. Adding 3 hours to 9:00 am gives 12:00 noon.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT section, Numerical Ability: HCF and LCM

subject: general_test
explanation: Convert to improper fractions: 2 1/3 = 7/3 and 1 3/4 = 7/4. Then 7/3 ÷ 7/4 = 7/3 x 4/7 = 4/3, and 4/3 x 3/8 = 12/24 = 1/2. Dividing by a fraction is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT section, Numerical Ability: Fractions and decimals

subject: general_test
stem: What is the value of 0.6 x 0.05 + 0.3 ÷ 0.1?
explanation: 0.6 x 0.05 = 0.03, because 6 x 5 = 30 and the two decimal places give 0.030. Also 0.3 ÷ 0.1 = 3, since 0.1 fits into 0.3 three times. The sum is 0.03 + 3 = 3.03.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT section, Numerical Ability: Fractions and decimals

subject: general_test
stem: What is the value of √1.44 + √0.0225?
ncert_ref: CUET GAT section, Numerical Ability: Squares and square roots

subject: general_test
stem: If x + 1/x = 5, what is the value of x² + 1/x²?
explanation: Square both sides: (x + 1/x)² = x² + 2 + 1/x². So x² + 1/x² = 5² - 2 = 25 - 2 = 23. Forgetting the middle term 2 gives 25.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT section, Numerical Ability: Squares and square roots (algebraic identities)

subject: general_test
stem: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 9?
explanation: A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 9. For 4,617 the digit sum is 4 + 6 + 1 + 7 = 18, which is divisible by 9. The other options have digit sums 15, 20 and 12, so none of them pass the test.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT section, Numerical Ability: Divisibility rules

subject: general_test
stem: What fraction of 1 kilogram is 350 grams? Give the answer in its simplest form.
explanation: 1 kilogram = 1,000 grams, so the fraction is 350/1,000. Dividing the numerator and the denominator by 50 gives 7/20. Since 350/1,000 and 7/20 are equal, the simplest form is the one that matches the options.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT section, Numerical Ability: Percentages and fractions

subject: general_test
stem: A rectangular field is 250 m long and 200 m wide. What is its area in hectares? (1 hectare = 10,000 m²)
explanation: Area = 250 x 200 = 50,000 m². Dividing by 10,000 m² per hectare gives 5 hectares. Treating 1 hectare as 1,000 m² gives 50 hectares, which is a unit slip.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT section, Numerical Ability: Unit conversion

subject: general_test
stem: Arrange the following in ascending order of their values: (A) 0.375 (B) 3/7 (C) 5/12 (D) 0.4. Choose the correct sequence from the options given below.
explanation: As decimals: 0.375, 3/7 ≈ 0.4286, 5/12 ≈ 0.4167 and 0.4. In ascending order the sequence is (A) 0.375, (D) 0.4, (C) 0.4167, (B) 0.4286. Writing each value to the same number of decimal places settles the comparison.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT section, Numerical Ability: Fractions, decimals and ordering

subject: general_test
stem: Evaluate: (-2)³ x (-3)² - 4² ÷ (-8)
explanation: (-2)³ = -8 and (-3)² = 9, so the product is -72. Next, 4² ÷ (-8) = 16 ÷ (-8) = -2. Subtracting -2 gives -72 - (-2) = -70. Powers come first, then division, then subtraction.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT section, Numerical Ability: Simplification (BODMAS and integers)

subject: general_test
stem: Consider the statements: (A) 2^10 = 1024. (B) √0.49 = 0.7. (C) The LCM of 6, 8 and 12 is 24. (D) 15% of 240 is 32. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
explanation: 2^10 = 1,024, so (A) is correct. 0.7 x 0.7 = 0.49, so (B) is correct. The LCM of 6, 8 and 12 is 24, so (C) is correct. 15% of 240 = 36, not 32, so (D) is false and the answer is (A), (B) and (C) only.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT section, Numerical Ability: Squares, roots, percentages and LCM

subject: general_test
stem: Find the letter that replaces the question mark in the series: A, C, F, J, O, ?
explanation: The gaps between the letters' positions in the alphabet increase by one each time: A(1), C(3), F(6), J(10), O(15). The next gap is 6, so the next position is 15 + 6 = 21, which is U.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Mental Ability: Number and letter series

subject: general_test
stem: Compass : Direction :: Barometer : ?
explanation: A compass is the instrument used to measure direction. A barometer is the instrument used to measure atmospheric pressure, so the analogy is Pressure.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Mental Ability: Analogies (instrument and quantity measured)

subject: general_test
stem: In a certain code, '+' means '×', '×' means '÷', '÷' means '−' and '−' means '+'. Using this code, what is the value of 18 + 6 × 3 ÷ 2 − 1? Solve from left to right.
explanation: Replace each symbol: 18 + 6 becomes 18 × 6 = 108. Then × 3 becomes ÷ 3, giving 36. Then ÷ 2 becomes − 2, giving 34. Finally − 1 becomes + 1, giving 35.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Mental Ability: Mathematical operations (symbol substitution)

subject: general_test
stem: If each letter of the word CHART is replaced by its position in the English alphabet (A = 1, B = 2 and so on) and the numbers are added, what is the total?
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Mental Ability: Alphabet position and letter coding

subject: general_test
stem: In a class, Meera is 15th from the top and 18th from the bottom when the students are ranked by height with no ties. How many students are in the class?
explanation: Counting Meera twice, the class has 15 + 18 − 1 = 32 students. The ranks from the top and from the bottom both include her position.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Mental Ability: Ranking and order

subject: general_test
stem: Find the next term in the series: 3, 4, 7, 11, 18, 29, ?
explanation: Each term is the sum of the two terms before it: 3 + 4 = 7, 4 + 7 = 11, 7 + 11 = 18 and 11 + 18 = 29. So the next term is 18 + 29 = 47.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Mental Ability: Number series (recurrence pattern)

subject: general_test
stem: Each row of the grid below follows the same rule. Row 1: 2, 3, 6. Row 2: 4, 5, 20. Row 3: 7, 2, ?. What number replaces the question mark?
explanation: In every row, the third number equals the first number multiplied by the second. Row 1 gives 2 × 3 = 6 and Row 2 gives 4 × 5 = 20. For Row 3, 7 × 2 = 14.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Mental Ability: Missing number in a grid (row rule)

subject: general_test
stem: Consider the letter pairs: AB, CD, FG, JK, ?. Which pair comes next in the series?
explanation: The first letters sit at alphabet positions 1, 3, 6, 10, and the gaps increase by 2, 3, 4. The next gap is 5, so the first letter is at position 15, which is O. The second letter is always one place after the first, so the pair is OP.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Mental Ability: Letter series (position gaps)

subject: general_test
stem: Which pair does not follow the same relationship as the other three pairs?
explanation: In 2 : 8, 3 : 27 and 5 : 125 the second number is the cube of the first (2³, 3³, 5³). In 4 : 16 the second number is the square of the first (4²), so this pair is the odd one out.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Mental Ability: Number relationships (powers)

subject: general_test
stem: Find the number that does not belong in the group: 121, 169, 225, 250.
explanation: 121 = 11², 169 = 13² and 225 = 15² are perfect squares. 250 is not a perfect square, so it does not belong.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, General Mental Ability: Odd one out (number properties)

subject: general_test
stem: Five people P, Q, R, S and T sit in a single row, all facing north. P sits at one end. Q sits immediately to the right of P. R sits at the other end. S sits between Q and R. T sits immediately to the left of R. Who sits in the middle?
explanation: Because Q is to the right of P, P must be at the left end (position 1). R is at the right end (position 5), so T is at position 4 and S is at position 3. Q is at position 2, which puts S in the middle.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical and Analytical Reasoning: Linear seating arrangement

subject: general_test
stem: Statements: P > Q ≥ R; S < R; T ≥ P. Conclusions: I. T > S. II. S > Q. III. P > R. Which conclusions follow?
explanation: From T ≥ P > Q ≥ R > S, we get T > S (I follows) and P > R (III follows). From S < R ≤ Q we get S < Q, so S > Q does not follow (II).
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical and Analytical Reasoning: Inequality reasoning

subject: general_test
stem: Six students P, Q, R, S, T and U are ranked by marks, with no ties. U scores more than S. S scores more than R. R scores more than P. P scores more than Q. Q scores more than T. Who is fourth from the top?
explanation: The statements give the full chain U > S > R > P > Q > T. The first four places are U, S, R and P, so P is fourth from the top.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical and Analytical Reasoning: Ranking and order

subject: general_test
stem: If 1 January 2025 was a Wednesday, what day of the week was 1 March 2025?
explanation: From 1 January to 1 March 2025 there are 31 days in January and 28 in February, which is 59 days. 59 leaves a remainder of 3 when divided by 7, so Wednesday moves forward 3 days to Saturday.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical and Analytical Reasoning: Calendar problems

subject: general_test
stem: Statements: All engineers are readers. Some readers are writers. No writer is a painter. Conclusions: I. Some engineers are writers. II. No engineer is a painter. Which of the following is correct?
explanation: The statements do not say whether any engineer is a writer, so I does not follow. Engineers are readers, but nothing links engineers to painters, so II does not follow either. Neither conclusion is forced.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical and Analytical Reasoning: Syllogisms (statement and conclusion)

subject: general_test
stem: Six people P, Q, R, S, T and U sit around a circular table, all facing the centre. P sits opposite S. Q sits immediately clockwise of P. R sits immediately counter-clockwise of S. U sits immediately clockwise of T. Who sits opposite Q?
explanation: Number the seats clockwise from P as seat 1. S is opposite P, so S is at seat 4. Q is at seat 2, and R, immediately counter-clockwise of S, is at seat 3. T and U fill seats 5 and 6 with U clockwise of T, so T is at seat 5. Seat 5 is opposite seat 2, which is Q, so T sits opposite Q.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical and Analytical Reasoning: Circular seating arrangement

subject: general_test
stem: A building has floors numbered 1 (ground floor) to 7. B lives on an even-numbered floor. C lives three floors above B and C lives on floor 5. A lives on the floor immediately above B. On which floor does A live?
explanation: C is on floor 5 and lives three floors above B, so B is on floor 2, which is even as required. A lives immediately above B, so A is on floor 3.
ncert_ref: CUET GAT syllabus, Logical and Analytical Reasoning: Floor and height puzzles

subject: general_test
stem: α and β are the roots of x² − 7x + 12 = 0. What is the value of α² + β²?
